title: TACTIC: Task-Aware Sparse Coordination Graphs for Multi-Task Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning
claim: A multi-stage system couples discrete trajectory abstraction with a frozen class predictor to drive sparse, task-conditioned coordination graphs.
layout: 3 colored regions (a)(b)(c), dense boxes and arrows, replay buffer to graph decomposition
description: A dense system diagram split into three tinted regions. Region (a), pale pink at top left, is Trajectory Clustering and Classifier Learning. It starts at an orange Replay Buffer cylinder and feeds a VQ-VAE with encoder and decoder trapezoids, a VQ-Codebook and a coverage loss. Quantized sequences go to K-means and then to a classifier f_psi trained with a cross-entropy loss. Region (b), pale yellow at bottom left, is Quantized Latent Space Generation. It holds a frozen goal predictor built from a GRU and MLPs, a one-hot encoding step and a trajectory-class representation model. Region (c), cyan at right, is Graph-based Decomposition. It shows a local agent network (MLP, GRU, MLP), a Q_tot mixing equation, and small colored agent graphs passing through Graph CONV and temporal smoothing. Boxed math symbols label nearly every arrow. A globe icon marks the environment and its joint actions.

abstract: Value factorization eases non-stationarity in MARL, but its static coordination assumptions hinder generalization on long-horizon tasks with shifting dependencies. Prior VQ-VAE methods abstract trajectories yet miss time-varying inter-agent dependencies. We present TACTIC, a CTDE framework with three components: (i) VQ-VAE-based trajectory abstraction that learns discrete task-semantic classes; (ii) semantic-conditioned sparse coordination graphs that adapt dependencies by pruning edges according to variance-based pairwise payoff sensitivity; and (iii) a pretrained, frozen trajectory-class predictor that conditions local policies while decoupling task recognition from control. On SMAC and SUMO, TACTIC shows strong overall competitiveness and adaptive coordination under sparse rewards and dynamic task structures.
